rows.title: corner-net coverage - the law, written BEFORE any corner letter
rows.was: Nothing for the corner. E51 gates the top MIDDLE pocket only. The corner census that reported three 15.6 x 10 mm openings was E51's dilated-bbox raster taken about the KERNEL cup centre, 27.7 mm off the net axis, with an AUTHORED 13 mm width threshold below the lattice's own MODEL plan diagonal 13.433 mm.
rows.now: E51c, five predicates on a written SCOPE. SCOPE S = { outward panel: |az| <= the outermost FLAP-HUNG column's azimuth (INSTRUMENT on the built column, 81.53 deg on 48fa8826, NOT the nominal phiHead - so it cannot drift when the plate window changes), y in [yRow1, yTopTable] } U { bag: y in [yTopTable - 1.1, yHem], all azimuths }. P1 (PRIMARY, graph-free) max clear opening <= 10.9 mm. P2 (never-cross) max clear opening < 52.5 mm. P3 max body-face inscribed diameter <= 12.7 mm. P4 max body-face area <= 169 mm2. P5 every body face is a quad and the only cylinder-wrapping faces are the two rims. NOT YET A BATTERY LETTER: P1/P2 are measurable from rendered bytes, P3/P4/P5 need the lattice graph decode. No corner letter is claimed this round; this row is the law the order required to exist first.
rows.provenance: D_max = 10.39 x 1.05 = 10.91 -> 10.9 mm [DERIVED]. 10.39 = the Magnum corner net's OWN largest clear opening on its leather panel [MODEL(Magnum), loops.npy cord-section centres per 1 mm level, cord radius 1.08 mm from MODEL(Magnum n1_cord) diameter 2.16, 0.4 mm grid, n = 77165 cells, at az 5.8 / z -33.6]; 1.05 = the Magnum's own cell dispersion p90/median = 1.0404 [MODEL(Magnum) knot-to-knot cell side median 11.897, p10 11.365, p90 12.378, n = 630] rounded up to the nearest 0.05. P2 52.5 mm = the snooker ball diameter [MFR / WPBSA]; implied by P1 with a 4.8x margin, written anyway. P3 12.7 = 12.14 x 1.05 [DERIVED; 12.14 = MODEL(Magnum) leather-side QUAD max inscribed diameter, n = 59]. P4 169 = 153.0 x 1.05^2 = 168.7 [DERIVED; 153.0 = MODEL(Magnum) quad max area, n = 59; area scales as the square of a linear tolerance]. P4 is NOT redundant with P3: a missing rung merges two cells vertically, doubling the area while leaving the inscribed circle unchanged. MAX and not p90 because a coverage law is a statement about the worst hole. Two Magnum faces (k=6 area 327.2 insc 15.41; k=7 area 456.0 insc 19.69) are EXCLUDED from the reference statistic as missed-knot merges in our read of the purchased model - a defect of the read, not of the net; the exclusion is conservative toward a FALSE RED on our net, never a false green. Operator validation: the measured median quad inscribed diameter 11.00 mm against the ideal rhombus incircle from the Magnum's own diagonals (plan 13.433, hang 19.266) = 11.02 mm, 0.2%. SEPARATION, all four cases through identical operators: (i) Magnum reference P1 10.39 / P3 12.14 / P4 153.0 PASS; (ii) our sealed 48fa8826 corner net P1 9.28 at az 72.9 / y -36.8 (n = 41184) / P3 11.91 / P4 157.7, 117/117 quads, wrapping faces = the two rims only, PASS with 15% headroom and 1.11 mm TIGHTER than the Magnum; (iii) one interior knot's four edges deleted P1 17.10 = 1.57x / P3 19.14 / P4 479.9, a k=8 face, FAIL x3; (iv) one whole course removed P1 21.92 = 2.01x / a new wrapping face k=42 insc 77.22 area 4995.0, FAIL x4. The law is insensitive to the tolerance over t in [1.00, 1.60]. NOTHING IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION because there is nothing to close: the three reported 15.6 x 10 mm openings measure 8.82 / 8.95 / 8.82 mm of clear opening in the net's own frame - no opening exists, and the earlier read is RETRACTED (its cause was a measurement frame 27.7 mm off axis plus a threshold below the MODEL quantum). The one construction change that would bridge the panel-edge STEP - dropping the R3-SNK-11 B3 hasHead guard on a head's outward legs - would run a single straight 68.9 mm cord, 5.8 MODEL cell sides, where M2 reads a step and the purchased model has no cord at all; it is refused. Raising headDeg past the MODEL 87 deg step azimuth, raising the table-side top edge off the MODEL(M2) -2.7 mm slab offset, and densifying NC past the MODEL plan diagonal are refused for the same reason: each authors a number over a measured one.

rows.title: two-directional, per the SNK-11 verification C-4
rows.was: one-directional: for every MODEL reference point, the distance to the nearest sample of ours. That is a COVERAGE test - material of OURS with no Magnum counterpart costs nothing.
rows.now: worse of the two directions. Both are computed inside the same measurement window (h > 0.5, -0.5 <= d <= 58); the JUDGED set is clipped to the window, never the TARGET set, so clipping cannot manufacture a near neighbour. NaN fails closed. The band [1.0, 2.0] is UNCHANGED - this is a completeness fix to the metric, not a re-tune. The letter now prints both directions, names the worse one, and discloses that our cut is taken at x 1434.5 mm against the Magnum's x 600. BOTH sides are now the same KIND of object, the VISIBLE OUTLINE. The Magnum fixture is one by construction: an OPEN 18-point trace of the bed, the undercut, the roll and the plateau out to the rail's outer top edge, which never turns back down. Our plane cut is CLOSED - it returns the cushion back and the cloth under the rail as well - so it is reduced to its own visible outline by two 0.25 mm silhouette ladders over the exact triangle-plane cut (FRONT = the smallest in-window d present at each height, TOP = the greatest h present at each depth); a sample is judged when it lies within VIS_EPS = 0.35 mm of one of them. The reduction is applied to our side in BOTH directions, target included: letting hidden material answer for a missing outline is the loose choice and this is the strict one. No point is invented - the judged set is a subset of our own cut samples.
rows.provenance: The one-way read answered 'is every part of the Magnum's section present in ours', not 'is our section the Magnum's section'. Symmetrising it is the standard completeness fix for a nearest-neighbour surface metric and introduces no new number. Tolerance basis unchanged: model facet noise 0.5 mm rms -> 2 sigma = 1.0 on p90; max 2.0 = the cap-seam / one-cloth-ply class. THE INSTRUMENT FINDING that building this direction produced, disclosed rather than clipped away: run raw, our closed section against the Magnum's open outline reads ours->ref p90 33.99 / max 36.40 mm, worst at d 50.7 h 3.3 - the cloth UNDER the rail, 50 mm outboard of the nose, invisible from the playing side and from above, and never described by the reference. That is an instrument mismatch, not a build defect; the unreduced read is printed beside the gate as a RECORD (E50cloud) together with the count of samples the reduction drops (412 of 924 in-window on the head tree). VIS_EPS 0.35: a surface at angle theta to the horizontal is missed by the top ladder by at most (VG/2)*tan(theta) and by the front ladder by at most (VG/2)*cot(theta); the smaller of the two is <= VG/2 = 0.125 mm for every theta, so 0.35 carries a 2.8x margin on the grid. RED ARM: on the e7ffa1c9 bytes the reduced read fires in BOTH directions - ref->ours p90 2.92 / max 5.12, ours->ref p90 1.64 / max 4.09 against a band of 1.0 / 2.0 - so the new direction is not inert and the reduction does not make a wrong section pass.

rows.provenance: The retired read and the retired value were both wrong, in opposite directions, and cancelled. The plank is a THREE.ExtrudeGeometry carrying railWoodOpts' 4.0 x 3.5 mm bevel with bevelOffset = -bevelSize, which insets the TOP FACE by bevelSize: the plan outline is the plank's MID-HEIGHT wall and stands 3.5 mm inboard of anything visible. The snooker plan never compensated it (cn8's wood plan does - BV in cn8LeftRailPlanHalves, the same 3.5 mm for the same reason), so the boundary stood at KIN + 3.5 = 54.17 while the letter that names it read the buried wall at 50.67 and passed. It survived review because the cushion loft's back line carried an authored 'topEnd + 3 mm' (retired this round under H6) that covered the bevel to d 53.11 - the +3 was a bevel compensation applied to the wrong body. Removing it exposed a 4.0 x 3.5 mm relief behind every cushion (E50 worst 0.77 -> 3.59 mm, 13 samples over 1 mm, every one on the bevel's own two facets). The plan now rides bevelSize inboard so the beveled top edge lands ON capInnerLip; MEASURED after the change: plan wall 47.67, top face 51.17, E50 worst back to 0.77. The 0.5 mm lap retires with it - MODEL(Magnum) reads the cap's inner lip 0.549 mm BEHIND the body's flat top end (sd 0.028, n = 15), an OPEN seam and not a lap; against the body's own topEnd back line the build reproduces it at 0.48 mm (delta 0.07), closing the residual this round had disclosed. Corroboration from a datum the Magnum read never touched: the plan wall 47.67 is the kernel SLATE EDGE (CW 47.625) to 0.045 mm - the capping seats on the frame just outboard of the slate. E31 is now also the drift detector for the bevel coupling: change railWoodOpts.bevelSize and it fires.
